skill.name: hubspot-integration
skill.description: Guidance for HubSpot CRM integrations, including OAuth, private app tokens, CRM objects, associations, batch operations, webhooks, and custom objects.
skill.summary: Plan secure HubSpot CRM integrations across authentication, data operations, and event workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no suspicious patterns in the single prompt-only SKILL.md file. Manual review found no prompt injection, executable code, network behavior, filesystem access, or secret handling instructions. No remediation is required.

content.value_statement: HubSpot CRM integrations require careful choices around authentication, records, associations, and sync design. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused patterns for safer implementation planning.
actual_capabilities: Outlines OAuth and private app token patterns for HubSpot integrations.
Describes CRM object create, read, update, and delete workflows.
Highlights HubSpot associations, batch operations, webhooks, and custom objects.
Covers usage patterns for Node.js and Python SDK implementations.
Calls out deprecated API keys, excessive individual requests, and polling risks.
limitations: Does not include runnable code, scripts, or automated setup.
Provides high-level patterns rather than full HubSpot API reference coverage.
Does not verify credentials, app scopes, or account-specific object schemas.
Requires users to check current HubSpot documentation for exact endpoint behavior.

use_cases.title: Plan a CRM Integration
use_cases.description: Map authentication, CRM object operations, associations, and sync boundaries before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Review Sync Architecture
use_cases.description: Compare batch operations, webhooks, and polling choices for reliable customer data movement.

use_cases.title: Create Implementation Guidance
use_cases.description: Turn HubSpot integration requirements into focused engineering notes for Node.js or Python teams.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how I should connect a new app to HubSpot CRM. Cover OAuth, private app tokens, and when each is appropriate.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new integration

prompt_templates.title: Plan CRM Workflows
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design HubSpot CRM object workflows for contacts, companies, and deals. Include associations and common failure points.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Sync Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my HubSpot sync plan. Recommend where batch operations and webhooks should replace individual requests or polling.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Integration Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this HubSpot integration design for authentication risks, object model gaps, webhook handling, and batch operation opportunities.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to authenticate a public HubSpot app.
output: Recommendation: use OAuth 2.0 for public apps.
Key checks: redirect handling, token refresh, required scopes, and secure token storage.
Avoid: deprecated API keys and shared private app tokens.

output_examples.input: A user asks why a contact sync is slow.
output: Likely issue: the design sends one request for each record.
Recommended path: group compatible operations into batches.
Additional check: use webhooks for change detection instead of frequent polling.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to model custom CRM data.
output: Start by identifying whether standard objects can represent the data.
Use custom objects when the entity needs its own lifecycle and associations.
Document association rules before writing import or sync logic.

best_practices: Use OAuth for public apps and private app tokens only for single-account integrations.
Batch compatible CRM operations to reduce rate pressure and improve sync reliability.
Use webhooks for change detection instead of frequent polling.
anti_patterns: Using deprecated API keys for new integrations.
Sending one API request per record when batch operations are available.
Polling CRM records when webhook subscriptions can deliver changes.

faq.question: Does this skill run HubSpot API calls?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance only and contains no executable code or network access.

faq.question: Which SDKs does it cover?
faq.answer: It references Node.js and Python SDK patterns for HubSpot CRM integrations.

faq.question: Can it help with custom objects?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help plan when custom objects are appropriate and how associations should be considered.

faq.question: Can it choose OAuth scopes?
faq.answer: It can help reason about scope categories, but users must confirm exact scopes in HubSpot.

faq.question: Is it safe for private app tokens?
faq.answer: It describes private app tokens for single-account integrations and does not request or store secrets.

faq.question: Does it replace HubSpot documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use it as implementation guidance and verify endpoint details in official HubSpot documentation.
